body: Energy measures the state and changes of physical systems. A falling object gives an example. In a model with negligible air resistance, the gravitational potential energy of the object–Earth system decreases while the object's kinetic energy increases.

Energy can transfer between systems. An object sliding to a stop on a rough surface warms the object and the surface, as some organized motion becomes internal energy. In an isolated system the total energy is conserved even as the form or location of the energy changes.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: The accounting depends on which objects and interactions are included in the system. The falling-object example uses an everyday mechanical approximation.
purpose: Distinguish conservation and energy transfer before discussing metabolism and machines.
